Rice Table IV summarizes historical Navy surveillance. Rice Table I covers a later series.

Both reports use the Pensacola Navy surveillance system. The series beginning January 1993 continues to April 2002 in Rice 2003 and April 2004 in Rice 2005. Individual cases and exposures have no crosswalk.
The 1993–1994 Pensacola series falls inside the Rice surveillance period. Case definitions and observation windows require reconciliation.

The two papers describe different session patterns and timing. Both use the same center. Individual-level linkage is unavailable.
USAF surveillance in 1985–1987 intersects with the period studied by Rush and Wirjosemito in their selected treated-trainee sample. The sampling frames and counting units differ.
McLoughlin also quotes the five historical 1983–1987 RAF cases reported by Harding. Its later one-year observation supplies a separate case and an approximate reported rate.
The Point Cook case period intersects the ADF training series beginning in 1984. Exposure-level linkage is unavailable.

The 1948 review quotes the 1946 cold-chamber study and misaligns the warm-group denominators. The 1946 original gives 122 exercise and 92 rest flights at 30,000 ft. The 1948 report also describes its own Pensacola series.
Israeli Air Force 2015–2019 surveillance falls within the 2015–2022 period of the later report. Matching events and role-specific exposure records are unavailable.

Both reports describe eight participants in the Polaris Dawn ground test at NASA JSC, comprising the four mission crew and four matched volunteers. The later paper also reports on a modified flight profile.
Both describe Italian Air Force training with similar profiles. The proceedings do not give a calendar window for the 1,777 trainees, so overlap with the 2003–2009 Morgagni series is unresolved.
